statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-39883 (GO-2026-5426, GHSA-hfvc-g4fc-pqhx): on BSD and Solaris, the host ID reader in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/resource runs the kenv command by bare name, so a manipulated PATH can run another program. It affects go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk v1.15.0 through v1.42.0 and is fixed in v1.43.0 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-hfvc-g4fc-pqhx, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5426). Inspected every published build of the alertmanager-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 36 builds, 0.31.1-r0 through 0.35.0-r2 (there is no 0.33.1-r4), on both x86_64 and aarch64, 72 packages, each verified against the repository index checksum. The payload of every package is two files, usr/bin/alertmanager and usr/bin/amtool: statically linked Go programs (no ELF interpreter) built for GOOS=linux with CGO_ENABLED=0. The function names the Go linker records in each binary (its function-name table) were searched, leaving out the standard library's own copies under vendor/golang.org/x/. The kenv call is in hostIDReaderBSD.read (https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/blob/v1.40.0/sdk/resource/host_id.go), and that reader is selected only by sdk/resource/host_id_bsd.go, whose build constraint is dragonfly || freebsd || netbsd || openbsd || solaris (https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/blob/v1.40.0/sdk/resource/host_id_bsd.go); on Linux the reader that reads /etc/machine-id is used. go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk is v1.40.0 in 0.31.1-r0 to 0.31.1-r5 and v1.43.0 or later from 0.31.1-r6. resource.New is linked into alertmanager, but no binary in any build contains the kenv command name, the smbios.system.uuid argument or the hostIDReaderBSD name. Positive control: the same search finds hostIDReaderLinux and the /etc/machine-id path in every binary. hostIDReaderBSD.read is defined in a file that is compiled on every platform, but on Linux nothing selects that reader, so the Go linker leaves it out: the vulnerable code is not present in any binary of this package.

CVE-2026-39883 (GO-2026-5426, GHSA-hfvc-g4fc-pqhx): the host ID detector in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/resource ran the BSD kenv command by bare name, so on DragonFly BSD, FreeBSD, NetBSD, OpenBSD and Solaris a kenv placed earlier in PATH could run in the application. The BSD reader, hostIDReaderBSD, is selected only by sdk/resource/host_id_bsd.go, whose build constraint names those platforms; v1.43.0 calls /bin/kenv instead: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/security/advisories/GHSA-hfvc-g4fc-pqhx, https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/pull/8113, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5426. Read the Go build information and the function table of every Go program in every build-dev package published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository: 89 builds, 2.6.4-r0 through the current 2.29.1-r1, each for x86_64 and aarch64 except 2.6.4-r0, which is published for aarch64 only, every download checked against the index checksum. Each package holds one file, the Go program /usr/bin/build. Version 2.19.1-r1 is listed three times in each index, every entry with the same source commit and installed size as 2.19.1-r0; the copy the repository serves was read. Every Go program in every build is built for GOOS=linux. /usr/bin/build links go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/resource, and the function table of every one contains the Linux reader, (*hostIDReaderLinux).read, which reads /etc/machine-id or /var/lib/dbus/machine-id and runs no command, but no build contains (*hostIDReaderBSD).read, the only code that runs kenv, or resource.New, the function the advisory lists. The vulnerable code is not in these programs. Builds before 2.20.0-r2 link go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk v1.38.0 or v1.40.0; 2.20.0-r2 and later link v1.43.0 or newer.

CVE-2026-39883 (GHSA-hfvc-g4fc-pqhx, GO-2026-5426): on BSD systems the OpenTelemetry-Go SDK's host-ID detector ran the kenv command without an absolute path, so a crafted PATH could run another program; it is an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-24051. It affects go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk from 1.15.0 up to, but not including, 1.43.0, and the Go vulnerability database lists resource.New in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/resource. Sources: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/security/advisories/GHSA-hfvc-g4fc-pqhx, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5426 and https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/releases/tag/v1.43.0. In the SDK source, the code that runs kenv is the read method of hostIDReaderBSD, which only sdk/resource/host_id_bsd.go uses, and that file is built only for DragonFly, FreeBSD, NetBSD, OpenBSD and Solaris; Linux builds use hostIDReaderLinux instead. We checked every published kube-state-metrics-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository as of 2026-11-27: 28 builds, 2.18.0-r0 to the current 2.20.0-r13, 54 packages, on x86_64 and aarch64 except 2.20.0-r7 and 2.20.0-r8, which were published for aarch64 only. Each package was downloaded and checked against its index checksum. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/kube-state-metrics, a statically linked Go program for Linux built with CGO_ENABLED=0, as its Go build information records (no program interpreter and no shared-library dependencies). Its build information lists go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk (v1.40.0 in 2.18.0-r0 to 2.18.0-r6, v1.43.0 in 2.19.0-r0 to 2.19.1-r2, v1.44.0 in 2.19.1-r3 to 2.20.0-r5, v1.46.0 in 2.20.0-r6 and v1.47.0 in 2.20.0-r7 to 2.20.0-r13). The Go function table of every build lists hostIDReaderLinux's read method but no hostIDReaderBSD function (runtime.main found in every build as a control), and a byte search of every build finds no occurrence of the string kenv, which the BSD code passes as the command name and uses in its error message. So the vulnerable code is not present in any build. Debian also marks golang-opentelemetry-otel not affected, as specific to BSDs and Solaris.

CVE-2026-39883 (GHSA-hfvc-g4fc-pqhx, GO-2026-5426): the OpenTelemetry Go SDK's host ID resource detector runs the kenv command by bare name, found through PATH, so on DragonFly BSD, FreeBSD, NetBSD, OpenBSD and Solaris a local attacker who controls PATH can run their own program in its place. It affects go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk 1.15.0 to 1.42.0 and is fixed in 1.43.0: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/security/advisories/GHSA-hfvc-g4fc-pqhx, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5426, https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/releases/tag/v1.43.0. The resource package source of go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk v1.40.0 is at https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/tree/sdk/v1.40.0/sdk/resource and v1.43.0, v1.44.0, v1.46.0 and v1.47.0 use the same build constraints: the host ID reader that calls kenv, hostIDReaderBSD, is installed only by host_id_bsd.go, which is built only for DragonFly BSD, FreeBSD, NetBSD, OpenBSD and Solaris, and the command helper it uses is in host_id_exec.go, built only for Darwin, the BSDs and Solaris; a Linux build installs hostIDReaderLinux from host_id_linux.go, which reads /etc/machine-id or /var/lib/dbus/machine-id and starts no command. We read every published metrics-server-dev package in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository: 29 builds, 0.8.1-r0 to 0.9.1-r2, each for x86_64 and aarch64, each verified against its index checksum. Each package installs a single file, /usr/bin/metrics-server, a statically linked Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0 and GOOS=linux; its Go build information, its Go function table and a raw byte search were read in every build. 0.8.1-r0 to 0.8.1-r6 contain go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk v1.40.0, inside the advisory's range, and 0.8.1-r7 and every later build contain v1.43.0 to v1.47.0, which carry the fix. In every build the function table lists (*hostIDReaderLinux).read among the go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/resource functions, but no hostIDReaderBSD or hostIDReaderDarwin method and no execCommand helper, and no build contains the byte string kenv or hostIDReaderBSD, while runtime.main is in every function table. No build has resource.New, the entry point the Go vulnerability database lists for this advisory, in its function table. The kenv code path is not in any published build.

CVE-2026-39883 (GHSA-hfvc-g4fc-pqhx, GO-2026-5426): on BSD and Solaris the OpenTelemetry Go SDK host ID detector runs kenv -q smbios.system.uuid by bare name, so a hostile PATH can substitute the command; go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk 1.15.0 up to but not including 1.43.0 is affected (https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/security/advisories/GHSA-hfvc-g4fc-pqhx, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5426). The kenv call is in hostIDReaderBSD.read in sdk/resource/host_id.go (https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/blob/sdk/v1.42.0/sdk/resource/host_id.go). That reader is selected only by sdk/resource/host_id_bsd.go, which carries the build constraint dragonfly || freebsd || netbsd || openbsd || solaris (https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/blob/sdk/v1.42.0/sdk/resource/host_id_bsd.go); a Linux build selects hostIDReaderLinux, which reads /etc/machine-id, and never references the BSD reader. This owner's packages for Alpine 3.23 are trivy-fips and trivy-fips-dev. Each installs one file, /usr/bin/trivy, a Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0 and GOOS=linux. All 38 published builds of each package (0.69.1-r0 to 0.74.0-r12) were downloaded on x86_64 and aarch64, 152 programs in all. Their Go build information shows go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk 1.40.0 to 1.42.0 in builds up to 0.69.3-r3 and 1.43.0 to 1.47.0 from 0.69.3-r4. A byte search of each whole program, which covers its symbol and function-name tables, finds no hostIDReaderBSD name and no smbios.system.uuid string in any of the 152 programs. The same search finds hostIDReaderLinux and /etc/machine-id in every one, and go tool nm lists the hostIDReaderLinux interface table in every one. The vulnerable code is therefore not present in any published build, whichever module version it embeds.

CVE-2026-39883 (GHSA-hfvc-g4fc-pqhx, GO-2026-5426): on BSD systems the OpenTelemetry-Go SDK's host-ID detector ran the kenv command without an absolute path, so a crafted PATH could run another program; it is an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-24051. It affects go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk from 1.15.0 up to, but not including, 1.43.0, and the Go vulnerability database lists resource.New in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk/resource. Sources: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/security/advisories/GHSA-hfvc-g4fc-pqhx, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5426 and https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/releases/tag/v1.43.0. In the SDK source, the code that runs kenv is the read method of hostIDReaderBSD, which only sdk/resource/host_id_bsd.go uses, and that file is built only for DragonFly, FreeBSD, NetBSD, OpenBSD and Solaris; Linux builds use hostIDReaderLinux instead. We checked every published kube-state-metrics-dev package for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository as of 2026-11-27: 23 builds, 2.18.0-5 to the current 2.20.0-13, 44 packages, on amd64 and arm64 except 2.20.0-7 and 2.20.0-8, which were published for arm64 only. The file list and MD5 manifest in each package's control archive show that its only file, /usr/bin/kube-state-metrics, has the same MD5 as the program in the DHI Alpine package of the same version and architecture (2.18.0-5 matches 2.18.0-r5, and so on), which we downloaded and checked against the Alpine index checksum, except the amd64 package of 2.20.0-4, which we downloaded in full: the file served did not match the repository index checksum on two downloads, so we read it as served; its program was built with the same Go release and module versions as the other 2.20.0-4 builds and gives the same result below. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/kube-state-metrics, a statically linked Go program for Linux built with CGO_ENABLED=0, as its Go build information records (no program interpreter and no shared-library dependencies). Its build information lists go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk (v1.40.0 in 2.18.0-5 to 2.18.0-6, v1.43.0 in 2.19.0-0 to 2.19.1-2, v1.44.0 in 2.19.1-3 to 2.20.0-5, v1.46.0 in 2.20.0-6 and v1.47.0 in 2.20.0-7 to 2.20.0-13). The Go function table of every build lists hostIDReaderLinux's read method but no hostIDReaderBSD function (runtime.main found in every build as a control), and a byte search of every build finds no occurrence of the string kenv, which the BSD code passes as the command name and uses in its error message. So the vulnerable code is not present in any build. Debian also marks golang-opentelemetry-otel not affected, as specific to BSDs and Solaris.
